Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Akhilesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Amit Kumar, learned State Law Officer and perused the record.
2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 384 of 2024, under Sections 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 67 of I.T. Act, Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: 3. The marriage of the informant was solemnized with a person in the district-Lakhimpur Kheri on 21.10.2017 and she had given birth to a baby girl out of the said marriage.
Subsequently, both are stated to have fallen apart, as such started living separately since 30.06.2023.
4. The victim is stated to have subsequently met the applicant and both started liking each other and came close and established relations as such.
The applicant on 15.08.2023 at about 2 p.m. is stated to have called the informant to his house to meet his parents, but reaching the house she did not find his parents.
5. The applicant is stated to have given her cold drink which was spiked and as such she was rendered unconscious.
She regained her consciousness at about 11 p.m. and found herself without any clothes.
The applicant revealed to the victim that he has committed rape with her and had taken an indecent video of her.

The victim regained her senses but she was forced to establish physical relationship again on the pretext that he shall make the said video viral.
6.
Subsequently, the victim is stated to have come back to her house and had severed her relations with the applicant and started doing a private job to take care of her daughter.
On 22.04.2024, it was revealed that her indecent video and photographs were posted on the Instagram ID of the applicant.

7. The victim is stated to have thereby called the applicant on his mobile no.9548540960 whereby he is stated to have told her that he has deliberately posted the said photographs on the Instagram as she had severed her relationship with him and had again asked her to establish corporeal relationship with him then only he shall delete the said photographs from Instagram.
As such, the FIR was instituted by the informant on 01.05.2024.

Arguments on behalf of applicant :
8. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
9. The FIR is delayed by about nine months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
10. The said allegation of applicant having raped her on 15.08.2023 stands falsified from the fact that the applicant was in jail since 09.07.2023 and was enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated 06.12.2023 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.41775 of 2023, as such the applicant is entitled for bail on the ground of his strong alibi.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.41775 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 11. The applicant has no criminal antecedents except a single case under section 376D/A of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act instituted at Police Station-Majhaula, District-Moradabad as Case Crime No.482 of 2023.
12. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

sentences.text: The applicant is languishing in jail since 02.06.2024 and the fundamental rights of the applicant stands violated.
As such, the applicant is entitled for bail.

Arguments on behalf of State :
14.

The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the statement of the victim recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. does not mention about the date of offence and there may be a discrepancy in mentioning the date of offence as there is a delay in instituting the FIR.
The instant case is just a misuse of the clout and power by the applicant as he had first clicked the indecent video and photographs of the victim and then posted them on Instagram.
15. The said act has been committed later on in the year 2024, as such, the alibi cannot be applied to the applicant.
The said photographs are indeed indecent and obscene and the applicant has posted them on Instagram as is evident as the same have been taken in possession by the Investigating Officer.

CONCLUSION :
16. The instant case indicates the mental depravity of the applicant coupled by the fact that although the applicant has been enlarged on bail in the said case, he has a criminal history of similar nature against him.
As such, the applicant does not deserve bail.

17. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, taking into consideration the fact that the applicant has made viral the indecent video and photographs of the victim on Instagram, there being a criminal history of similar nature assigned to him and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
18. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

19. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
